headline: Giant Anteater Population Rebounds in Argentina After Nearly Two Decades
meta_description: Nearly 20 years after Argentina began reintroducing giant anteaters to the Iberá Wetlands, the population has grown from zero to around 200 individuals.
summary_short: A pioneering reintroduction project in Argentina has successfully restored giant anteaters to a landscape where they vanished decades ago, growing from zero to 200.
body:
What began as a daring experiment in 2007 has blossomed into a conservation triumph: the giant anteater population in Argentina's Iberá Wetlands has grown from zero to approximately 200 individuals, marking nearly two decades of steady success for one of the world's first large-scale reintroduction efforts. La Fundación Rewilding Argentina initiated the project in the Corrientes province, where the species—locally known as yurumí—had disappeared by the mid-20th century due to poaching, habitat degradation, and fires. Over the years, 110 giant anteaters were rescued, rehabilitated, and released into the wetlands, many of them orphaned or individuals who had wandered dangerously close to human settlements.

What sets this recovery apart is not merely the numbers, but the self-sustaining nature of the population. Many of the reintroduced anteaters have bred successfully, creating multiple generations of wild-born, wild-raised animals that thrive in their restored habitat—animals that never knew captivity and are fully suited to wetland life. The steady growth demonstrates that the species can genuinely reclaim its former home when given the chance.

The ripple effects of this success extend far beyond a single species. The methodology that La Fundación Rewilding Argentina refined through the anteater project now serves as a blueprint for restoring other key predators and herbivores across different ecosystems, including the Iberá itself. What started as an audacious attempt to reverse extinction in one corner of South America has become a model for rewilding efforts worldwide—proof that with patience, careful planning, and commitment, landscapes and the creatures that belong to them can be reunited.
quick_facts: Giant anteaters reintroduced to Iberá Wetlands in Corrientes, Argentina in 2007
Population grew from 0 to approximately 200 individuals in nearly 20 years
110 anteaters rescued and rehabilitated for release into the wild
Species had vanished from region by mid-20th century due to poaching and habitat loss
Project methodology now used as model for restoring other species globally
